strengths: Addresses a novel and highly practical challenge in human avatar reconstruction: synthesizing sharp, animatable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) avatars directly from motion-blurred multi-view videos.
Proposes a physically grounded 3D blur-formation model that integrates 3DGS and the SMPL parametric body model, mapping sub-frame motion sequences to synthesized blurry observations.

Utilizes a well-designed 3D human motion model, combining B-spline pose interpolation, a continuous pose deformation model, and an inter-frame geodesic pose regularization loss to successfully resolve temporal and directional ambiguities inherent in motion blur.

Validates the method thoroughly on both a synthetic benchmark (derived from ZJU-MoCap) and a custom real-world dataset captured with a synchronous multi-view hybrid-exposure system, showing clear quantitative and qualitative improvements over existing 2D-deblurring + 3D-reconstruction pipelines.
weaknesses: The approach is heavily reliant on the SMPL model constraint, which limits its ability to handle complex geometries that lie outside the SMPL topology, such as loose clothing, long hair, or handheld objects.

The computational overhead and optimization time of the proposed joint optimization (which fits B-spline control knots, CNN-based pose displacement, LBS weights, shape parameters, and 3DGS properties) are not clearly discussed or compared against standard baselines.

The physical modeling of camera blur is simplified by averaging directly in the non-linear sRGB space rather than the linear radiance space, which may lead to artifacts in highly saturated or high-contrast regions as noted in the limitations.

strengths: Proposes a novel and physically-grounded formulation to reconstruct sharp, animatable 3D human avatars directly from motion-blurred multi-view/monocular videos.

Integrates a 3D-aware human motion model based on B-spline interpolation, pose deformation networks, and inter-frame temporal regularization to resolve motion ambiguities (such as temporal ordering and direction).

Outstanding experimental validation with a custom-built 360-degree hybrid-exposure camera system that captures high-quality real-world synchronized blurry/sharp pairs, alongside extensive synthetic experiments.

Provides thorough ablation studies, evaluating every aspect of the pipeline including trajectory representation (B-spline vs Slerp vs Linear), initialization perturbation, number of training views, and mask quality.
weaknesses: The computational complexity of the joint optimization is likely high, as it requires rendering T virtual frames per exposure period to synthesize each blurry frame. A discussion on optimization runtime compared to standard avatar reconstruction methods is missing.

The blur model averages colors in the non-linear sRGB space instead of the linear radiance space, which is physically inaccurate (as noted in limitations). Evaluating the impact of linearizing the images before averaging would provide more insights.

strengths: The paper addresses a highly practical and novel problem: reconstructing high-quality, animatable 3D human avatars directly from motion-blurred multi-view videos.

The proposed formulation integrates a physics-based 3D blur formation model with a 3D human motion model (using B-splines and a pose deformation network) to successfully resolve motion ambiguities (e.g., temporal ordering and direction).

The authors build a high-quality real-world benchmark using a custom 360-degree synchronous hybrid-exposure camera system (comprising sharp and blurry synchronized cameras) which provides a solid ground-truth evaluation for real-world deblurring.
Comprehensive experimental results show significant improvements over two-stage baselines (applying SOTA 2D video deblurring followed by 3D Gaussian Splatting) both quantitatively and qualitatively.

Extensive ablation studies and robustness analyses are provided, evaluating parameters like the number of control points, trajectory types, number of training views, and sensitivity to initialization perturbations.
weaknesses: The training complexity and computational overhead are not thoroughly discussed. Since the model renders multiple virtual sharp frames (e.g., $T=5$) per exposure to compute the blur loss, the training time and GPU memory usage are likely scaled up. Quantitative details on training time comparisons would make the paper stronger.

The dependence on coarse SMPL initializations is a potential bottleneck. Although the method shows robustness to random perturbations, it would be beneficial to discuss failure modes where the initial pose estimate is excessively distorted by severe blur.
Some implementation details are missing or brief, such as the exact architecture and inputs of the CNNs used for pose displacement ($G_{disp}$) and LBS weight refinement ($\delta$).

strengths: Introduces a novel formulation for reconstructing sharp, animatable 3D human avatars from multi-view motion-blurred videos, elegantly extending 3D-aware deblurring to dynamic, articulated subjects.
Combines a physics-based 3D blur formation model with SMPL body priors, B-Spline pose interpolation, and non-rigid displacements to successfully constrain a highly ill-posed optimization problem.
Addresses the inherent motion direction ambiguity under motion blur by proposing an effective inter-frame motion regularization term ($L_{reg}$).
Validates the approach thoroughly on both a synthetic benchmark and a realistic real-world dataset captured with a synchronous, hybrid-exposure multi-camera system.
Demonstrates clear quantitative and qualitative improvements over two-stage baselines (2D deblurring + dynamic 3DGS representation).
weaknesses: There is a noticeable copy-paste duplication error in Section 2.1 (Related Work, column 2, page 2), where the paragraph starting with 'In recent years, the deblurring paradigm...' is almost identically repeated.

The method heavily depends on pre-computed masks (e.g., from Segment-Anything) to isolate the human subject. It struggles to model the boundary blending between foreground and background caused by motion blur, which is a key limitation.

The paper lacks a discussion on the computational complexity and optimization time. Specifically, rendering $T$ virtual frames per training step to simulate blur is likely to increase training time and GPU memory consumption significantly compared to standard GauHuman.

There is a potential dependency on the quality of the initial SMPL parameters. It remains unclear how robust the bundle-adjustment process is to highly degraded initial pose estimates under severe blur.

strengths: Addresses a highly practical and challenging problem: reconstructing high-quality, animatable 3D human avatars from multi-view videos affected by motion blur.

Formulates a sound 3D-aware blur formation model specifically designed for humans, integrating 3D Gaussian Splatting, SMPL motion modeling, B-spline pose interpolation, and non-rigid pose deformations.
Introduces an effective inter-frame motion regularization loss ($L_{reg}$) that successfully resolves motion direction ambiguity and enforces temporal consistency.

Constructs a high-quality real-captured multi-view dataset using a unique hybrid-exposure camera system (synchronizing long-exposure/ND-filtered blurry cameras with short-exposure sharp cameras) which serves as a solid benchmark.
Demonstrates clear and significant improvements, both quantitatively and qualitatively, over standard 2D deblurring baselines combined with 3D reconstruction models.
weaknesses: There is a major editing oversight in Section 2.1 (Related Work: Image & Video Deblurring), where two large paragraphs starting with 'In recent years, the deblurring paradigm...' and 'Recently, the advent of 3D technologies...' are repeated almost verbatim in the same column.

The formulation of the normalized time in Eq. 10 uses $t/T$ where $t \in [0, T-1]$. This means the normalized time interval never reaches $1.0$ (maximum value is $(T-1)/T$). It should likely be normalized by $T-1$ to cover the full range $[0, 1]$ of the exposure period.

The technical novelty is somewhat incremental, as it largely adapts the formulation of 'Bad-Gaussians' (Zhao et al.) to the human avatar case by utilizing SMPL and LBS. However, the adaptation is well-tailored and non-trivial.

The method's robustness to poor initial SMPL estimates is not fully discussed. Under severe blur, off-the-shelf pose estimators (like EasyMoCap) might produce highly erroneous initialization. It would be helpful to analyze how the joint optimization behaves under such catastrophic initialization errors.

strengths: Practical and Significant Problem: Reconstructing animatable 3D human avatars from real-world videos is often hindered by motion blur. Addressing this issue directly improves the applicability of 3DGS-based human reconstruction in casual capture scenarios.

Physically Grounded 3D-Aware Blur Formulation: The proposed method integrates the physics of camera exposure into the 3D human deformation pipeline by rendering and averaging virtual intermediate frames. This is a mathematically sound way to model motion-induced blur.

Comprehensive Motion Modeling: Utilizing B-splines for sub-frame pose interpolation combined with a non-rigid displacement model and inter-frame regularization successfully resolves the temporal ambiguity of motion-induced blur.

Real-world Evaluation Benchmark: The authors constructed a high-quality, synchronous hybrid-exposure multi-view camera system to collect a real-world dataset. This is a valuable contribution to the community.

Thorough Experimental Validation: The method shows significant improvements over competitive 2-stage (2D deblurring + 3D reconstruction) baselines. The ablation studies are comprehensive, analyzing each design component and hyperparameter (e.g., the number of control knots P, virtual sharp frames T, and blur magnitude).
weaknesses: Severe Text Duplication: There is a major text duplication on Page 2 and Page 3. The entire Section 2.1 (Image & Video Deblurring) is repeated twice, with the second instance cutting off and continuing at the top of Page 3. This indicates a lack of final proofreading before submission.

Incremental Technical Novelty: The concept of modeling camera exposure through sub-frame rendering and averaging is heavily inspired by existing deblurring NeRF/3DGS works (e.g., Bad-NeRF, Bad-Gaussians). While adapting it to the SMPL-guided 3DGS framework for human avatars is logical and works well, the core conceptual novelty is somewhat limited.

Sensitivity to Coarse SMPL Initialization: The method relies on an initial estimation of SMPL parameters (e.g., from EasyMoCap) on blurry images. Since motion blur severely degrades keypoint detection and pose estimation, the paper would benefit from an analysis of how robust the joint optimization is to poor initial pose estimates.

Modeling of Background Blending: The current formulation does not handle foreground-background blending at the silhouette boundaries caused by sub-frame motion. While acknowledged as a limitation, this still restricts the visual quality of the boundaries in scenes with complex backgrounds.
